title: How Marco Rubio Is Running Venezuela From Afar
partialText: The secretary of state effectively controls Venezuela’s finances, the distribution of its natural resources and its government. His grip on the country is a vivid manifestation of American power in the Trump era.

title: Times Journalists Subpoenaed as Trump Escalates Pressure on Media
partialText: The Justice Department is seeking to compel testimony from reporters who wrote about the new Air Force One. The Times called the move a “brazen act.”

title: What We Know About the ICE Shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo
partialText: Mr. Araujo was a father, a husband and a business owner who had moved to the United States 35 years ago from Mexico.

title: Whistle-Blowers Accuse Kennedy Center of Contracting Flaws Under Trump
partialText: Documents submitted to Congress detailed concerns about competitive bidding processes and a White House order to tear up new bathroom tile because of its color.

title: Platner’s Rise and Fall Revives Old Questions About ‘Bernie Bros’ and Women
partialText: The collapse of Graham Platner’s Senate bid in Maine after a rape allegation renewed attention to a movement built by Senator Bernie Sanders that some say is too forgiving of male misconduct.

title: How The Times Reported on Graham Platner
partialText: Two senior editors discuss the difficult effort to track down allegations against the leading Democrat for Senate in Maine and the questions that soon followed.

title: An American Politician is Blocked by Israeli Settlers in the West Bank
partialText: Representative Ro Khanna was barred from leaving for 90 minutes. Where past U.S. leaders toured the region to show support for Israel, today’s Democratic presidential aspirants are going to bolster their credentials as critics.

title: Kansans Will Vote on an Elected Supreme Court. The Target: Abortion.
partialText: Frustrated by the appointed court’s support of abortion rights, which has been affirmed resoundingly by voters, Republicans are pushing an Aug. 4 referendum to elect Kansas justices.

title: Israel Struck an Iranian Steel Facility. Was It a Valid Military Target?
partialText: During the war, Israel attacked Iran’s steel plants, saying they provided forces with revenue and the means to make weapons, but it also hurt the civilian economy.

title: Iran’s Top Diplomat Is in Oman for Talks on Strait as Ayatollah Vows Revenge
partialText: The visit comes after heavy clashes this week between the U.S. and Iran. The country’s supreme leader pledged to avenge his father’s killing, trading threats with President Trump.

title: Buckling Manhattan High Rise Becomes Focus of Criminal Investigation
partialText: The inquiry, being conducted by the New York City Department of Investigation and the Manhattan district attorney’s office, was in an early stage, and its focus was unclear.

title: Developer of Troubled Midtown High-Rise Had Tried to Avoid the Spotlight
partialText: Nathan Berman has shied away from the showy ways necessary to succeed in New York real estate. Now, his largest project is in limbo.

title: Mick Jagger Knows He May Have Played His Last Rolling Stones Show
partialText: The legendary rock star, now 82, on how fame, touring and aging have changed him.

title: We’re Living in a Tick Nightmare. It’s Time to Go to War.
partialText: With ticks, we’ve barely begun to fight back. The longer we wait, the more territory they will claim across both our geographic and psychic maps.

title: The Population Forecasts Are Grim. They’re Still Too Optimistic.
partialText: America is not prepared for population decline.

title: Gravitational Pull
partialText: We think and dream and fuss and project entire worlds into existence. Meanwhile, the earth’s orbit continues and the sun goes on shining.

title: Non-Disclosure: In Roswell, New U.F.O. Docs Are a Declassified Bummer
partialText: Roswell’s annual U.F.O. festival was supposed to be full of triumphant “told you so’s” after the Trump administration declassified its alien files. Instead, apparently, the coverup continues.
